1.title: The Two Ways
1.text: The psalter opens by showing the difference between the godly and the ungodly, that we may rightly discern our own way. The blessed man avoids three steps of declension — walking, standing, sitting in the way of sinners — and instead delights in the law of the Lord, meditating on it day and night. He is like a tree planted (not wild), well-rooted by streams, fruitful in season, with leaves that do not wither. The way of the wicked, by contrast, shall perish. God knows his people.

23.title: The Lord My Shepherd
23.text: Believers may say, 'The Lord is my Shepherd.' One word here changes everything: 'my.' From this flow all the comforts of the psalm. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures — quiet rest in plenty. He restoreth my soul, when wandering or fainting. He leads in paths of righteousness, not for any merit in us, but for his name's sake. Even in the valley of death's shadow we fear no evil, for he is with us, his rod and staff comforting. The cup runs over; goodness and mercy follow us; we shall dwell in the house of the Lord forever.

51.title: A Penitent's Plea
51.text: David, convicted of his sin with Bathsheba, pleads not on his merits but on God's tender mercies. He acknowledges sin in three ways — transgression, iniquity, sin — and confesses against God only is he ultimately accountable. His petition is twofold: cleanse me, and create in me a clean heart. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart he will not despise. Repentance restores the joy of salvation and equips the believer to teach transgressors God's ways.
